1	/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
2	 *
3	 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
4	 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
5	 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
6	 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
7	 *
8	 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
9	 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
10	 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
11	 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
12	 *
13	 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
14	 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
15	 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
16	 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
17	 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
18	 * between the markers.
19	 */
20	
21	#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
22	#define ANDESIM_ROI_H
23	
24	static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
25	{
26	  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
27	}
28	
29	static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
30	{
31	  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
32	}
33	
34	#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */

2	
3	Workspace for the Andes hybrid simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz) + vsim
4	(SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) sharing memory and architectural state
5	across a magic-CSR boundary.
6	
7	Submodule:
8	
9	- `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
10	  contract under `include/hybrid/`, shared by the plugin, the driver, and vsim.
11	
12	QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries (set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` and
13	`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env`; see `config.env.example`), not vendored as
14	submodules. vsim sources live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo, built there.
15	
16	## Quickstart
17	
18	```sh
19	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim && cd hybrid_sim
20	bash scripts/build_all.sh
21	bash scripts/test_all.sh
22	```
23	
24	Subcommands: `run`, `profile`, `list`, `doctor`. Run `./andesim -h` for the
25	full list. `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` is the end-user guide: first runs on
26	each model, then every `run` option one by one.
27	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine <id>` prints the
28	hybrid-supported guest memory map (USER_GUIDE section 5.5).
29	
30	## Host dependencies
31	
32	- C/C++ toolchain (clang preferred), CMake >= 3.20, ninja
33	- Python 3
34	- glib-2.0 dev (for the QEMU plugin)
35	- pkg-config

43	After `bash scripts/build_all.sh`:

45	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotIterationLoop.so`, the `andesim profile` plugin)

1	# andesim User Guide
2	
3	Audience: an engineer who wants to RUN programs on the Andes simulators
4	through `./andesim` and measure cycle counts. This guide covers every
5	user-facing option and feature.
6	
7	It assumes andesim and its engines are already installed and built
8	(QEMU, the vsim engines, the plugin, the runtime, and the test ELFs are
9	prebuilt). If something is missing, run `./andesim doctor` and hand the
10	report to whoever owns your install; building is covered in `README.md`,
11	not here.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. What andesim is
16	
17	andesim runs one RISC-V ELF on one of three models:
18	
19	| Model    | What runs                              | Speed          | You get                    |
20	|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
21	| `fast`   | QEMU only (functional)                 | MHz-class      | program output, fast        |
22	| `cycle`  | one cycle-accurate engine, from reset  | kHz-class      | program output + total cycles |
23	| `hybrid` | QEMU fast-forwards, then the cycle engine measures one region you choose | fast until your region | program output + cycles of JUST your region |
24	
25	`hybrid` is the headline feature: QEMU races through boot and setup, then
26	hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate
27	engine (vsim, built from the real RTL), which runs only your
28	region-of-interest (ROI). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta
29	across that window. You mark the window with a **trigger**: source-level
30	markers or a pair of PCs (section 5.3).
31	
32	One run models ONE core. The cycle engine defines the hardware (ISA,
33	VLEN, caches); in hybrid mode the QEMU leg automatically inherits that
34	engine's ISA and VLEN so both legs execute the same architecture.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 2. Check your installation
39	
40	```sh
41	./andesim doctor          # read-only health report
42	./andesim list models     # the three models
43	./andesim list engines    # every engine you can pass to --engine
44	```
45	
46	`doctor` checks artifacts, toolchain, runtime, engines, and the shared-memory
47	backing tiers, and prints WSL2 advice where relevant. A healthy install ends
48	with `Summary: N PASS, 0 FAIL`.
49	
50	`list engines` shows what `--engine` accepts:
51	
52	```
53	ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN
54	qemu64                 qemu  functional      64    -     -     -
55	qemu32                 qemu  functional      32    -     -     -
56	vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
57	vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  64    512   512   32
58	```
59	
60	`qemu64`/`qemu32` are the functional engines (`fast`); the `vsim:<cfg>`
61	entries are the cycle-accurate engines (`cycle`, and the measuring leg of
62	`hybrid`). `-` means the engine does not report that parameter.
63	
64	Run `./andesim run -h` any time for the compact flag list; this guide is
65	the long version.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 3. First runs
70	
71	The install ships ready-made ELFs under `tests/fixtures/`; the examples
72	below use them. Replace with your own ELF once you have one (section 4).
73	
74	### 3.1 fast -- functional, full speed
75	
76	```sh
77	./andesim run --mode fast tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
78	```
79	
80	```
81	hello from vplat
82	```
83	
84	Output is the program's own output, verbatim (QEMU passthrough). The exit
85	code of your program becomes the process exit code.
86	
87	### 3.2 cycle -- one engine, from reset, total cycles
88	
89	```sh
90	./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf
91	```
92	
93	```
94	hello from vplat
95	[andesim] 4247 cycles
96	```
97	
98	The engine's startup banner and verbose info log are filtered out so the
99	result stands alone; real warnings/errors still pass through, and the
100	program's exit code is propagated. The figure is the whole run from reset
101	-- boot, runtime init, everything.
102	
103	### 3.3 hybrid -- fast-forward, then measure your region
104	
105	`hybrid` needs a trigger that says where the measured window starts and
106	ends. The fixture below already contains ROI markers, so `--trigger
107	marker` works out of the box:
108	
109	```sh
110	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
111	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
112	```
113	
114	```
115	hello from QEMU1
116	[andesim] 54 cycles
117	```
118	
119	Reading the output:
120	
121	- `hello from QEMU1` is the program's own output from the fast leg.
122	- `[andesim] 54 cycles` is the answer: your ROI took 54 cycles on
123	  this engine. It is the vsim `mcycle` delta across the window (the same
124	  line shape `cycle` mode prints, but here it covers JUST your ROI).
125	- The run ends after the ROI. Code after your ROI never executes in a
126	  hybrid run -- hybrid is a measuring tool, not a way to finish the program.
127	- Want more detail? `--log-level 1` (section 5.10) adds the driver's
128	  chatter: the resolved engine/VLEN/trigger banner and the shared-memory
129	  line (`[andesim] mmap ...`, section 5.4).
130	
131	The first hybrid run of a given (engine, ELF) pair is a few seconds slower:
132	andesim captures the engine's reset state once and caches it under
133	`~/.cache/andesim/` so later runs can skip restoring registers that still
134	hold reset values (typically ~4x faster on the vsim leg). The cache
135	refreshes itself when the engine or the ELF changes.

139	## 4. Prepare your own program
140	
141	### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine
142	
143	Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
144	and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:
145	
146	```sh
147	riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
148	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
149	```
150	
151	- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
152	- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
153	  compiling outside the repo.
154	- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
155	  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
156	  semihosting library can leak into the link.
157	- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.
158	
159	For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:
160	
161	```sh
162	riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
163	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
164	```
165	
166	C++ works through the same two flags -- just switch the driver to `g++`:
167	
168	```sh
169	riscv64-unknown-elf-g++ -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
170	  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.cpp -o your_prog.elf
171	```
172	
173	- Static constructors run before `main` (crt0 walks `.init_array` via
174	  newlib's `__libc_init_array`), and returning from `main` has C++
175	  `exit(rc)` semantics: atexit handlers and static destructors run.
176	- libstdc++ heap containers (`std::string`, `std::vector`, ...) sit on
177	  the runtime heap; the g++ driver adds `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, and the
178	  specs add `crtbegin/crtend`.
179	- Prefer `printf` over `<iostream>`: iostreams add hundreds of KB of
180	  code and static-init work that noticeably lengthens a cycle-mode boot.
181	
182	Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:
183	
184	```sh
185	... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
186	  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
187	  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
188	```
189	
190	(For C++, add `crtbegin.o`/`crtend.o` around your objects and `-lstdc++
191	-lm` before the group -- or just use the `g++` driver form above.)
192	
193	What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:
194	
195	| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
196	|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
197	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
198	| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
199	| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |
200	
201	A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
202	to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.
203	
204	### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)
205	
206	For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:
207	
208	```c
209	#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */
210	
211	andesim_ROI_begin();
212	my_kernel(a, b, c);
213	andesim_ROI_end();
214	```
215	
216	The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
217	binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
218	Ship one binary; measure when you want.
219	
220	> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
221	> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
222	> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
223	> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
224	> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
225	> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
226	> compiler.
227	
228	### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries
229	
230	`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
231	`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
232	the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the profile command:
233	
234	```sh
235	./andesim profile --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
236	```
237	
238	It runs the binary fast (QEMU, configured like your engine) and reports
239	the hottest loops (function, source line, PCs) with a ready `measure:`
240	line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair you can paste straight into the
241	hybrid command. See section 6 and `docs/profile.md` for the full flag
242	reference.

246	## 5. The `run` options, one by one
247	
248	Synopsis:
249	
250	```
251	./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]
252	```
253	
254	`run` is the default command -- you may omit it. `./andesim --mode fast
255	my.elf` and `./andesim my.elf --mode fast` both work; only the explicit
256	commands (`profile`, `list`, `doctor`) are recognized by name.
257	
258	### 5.1 `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` (required)
259	
260	Picks the model (section 1). Everything else keys off this choice.
261	
262	### 5.2 `--engine <id>`
263	
264	Picks the engine from `./andesim list engines`.
265	
266	- `fast`: optional. The driver auto-selects `qemu64` or `qemu32` to match
267	  your ELF's width; an explicit `--engine qemu32|qemu64` overrides (with a
268	  warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
269	- `cycle` / `hybrid`: names the cycle-accurate engine. Optional only when
270	  exactly one is installed; with several you must choose:
271	
272	  ```
273	  andesim run --mode cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines;
274	  select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced)
275	  ```
276	
277	Width rules: `cycle`/`hybrid` reject an ELF whose width does not match the
278	engine, up front:
279	
280	```
281	andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
282	  -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
283	```
284	
285	Hybrid additionally requires an rv64 engine (the fast leg is rv64; an rv32
286	engine cannot share architectural state with it and is rejected).
287	
288	VLEN: each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN (see `list engines`); in hybrid
289	mode the QEMU leg inherits the engine's ISA and VLEN automatically, so
290	both legs execute identical architecture. Supported VLEN range in hybrid:
291	128 to 1024 bits. A standalone `fast` run defaults to the vector-capable
292	`andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32) CPU model; to pin an exact
293	VLEN there, append a `-cpu` through the passthrough tail (the last `-cpu`
294	wins):
295	
296	```sh
297	./andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256
298	```
299	
300	### 5.3 `--trigger marker|pc` (+ `--pc-start`, `--pc-end`) -- hybrid only, required
301	
302	The ROI delimiter for `--mode hybrid`.
303	
304	**`--trigger marker`** (recommended when you can edit the source): the
305	window is the span strictly between `andesim_ROI_begin()` and
306	`andesim_ROI_end()` (section 4.2). The markers themselves are NOPs and
307	cost nothing.
308	
309	**`--trigger pc`**: explicit boundaries, no source edits. Both flags are
310	required; each accepts a symbol name or a `0x` hex address:
311	
312	```sh
313	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
314	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc my.elf
315	```
316	
317	Semantics you should know:
318	
319	- The instruction at `--pc-start` executes INSIDE the measured window (the
320	  fast leg stops just before it; the cycle engine resumes at it -- no
321	  instruction is lost across the handoff). `--pc-end` is where the window
322	  closes.
323	- Symbols are resolved from the ELF's own symbol table by the driver; no
324	  toolchain is needed at run time. A name that is not defined fails with
325	  `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>`; a bad literal fails with
326	  `malformed address '<x>'`.
327	- Both triggers are one-shot: the first hit of the start boundary opens the
328	  window, the first hit of the end boundary closes it. For a function called
329	  many times, the window is the FIRST call.
330	- Start and end must resolve to different addresses; an equal pair is an
331	  empty window and is rejected up front:
332	  `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address 0x... (an empty ROI measures nothing)`.
333	
334	### 5.4 `--mem-size <spec>` -- guest memory
335	
336	`SPEC` accepts `256M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes. Per-model meaning:
337	
338	| Model    | Effect |
339	|----------|--------|
340	| `hybrid` | Your program RAM (default `128M`). Max `2G` minus 4 KiB: the driver reserves one page just above your RAM for the vector-register transport, so exactly `2G` is rejected (use `2047M`) and an ELF whose static image reaches into the reserved page is rejected with `raise --mem-size or shrink the image`. |
341	| `fast`   | Forwarded as a plain QEMU `-m`. No 2G cap; QEMU validates the size itself. |
342	| `cycle`  | Ignored (the engine always models its full DRAM window); the driver says so on stderr. |
343	
344	Where the hybrid shared memory lives: andesim allocates a file both legs
345	map. It picks the first tier with enough free space (request + 256 MiB
346	headroom); run with `--log-level 1` to see which:
347	
348	1. `/dev/shm` -- RAM-backed, fastest.
349	2. `~/.cache/andesim` -- disk-backed fallback (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
350	
351	```
352	[andesim] mmap 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
353	```
354	
355	Set `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` to pin one directory with NO fallback past it
356	(the run fails with a hint if it cannot hold the request). Do not pin a
357	tmpfs mount (`/tmp` on some distros) expecting a disk ceiling -- tmpfs is
358	still RAM.
359	
360	### 5.5 `--print-memmap` -- which addresses may a hybrid workload touch?
361	
362	Prints the guest memory map for exactly the run you are about to do (same
363	`--engine`/`--mem-size`; the ELF is optional and only adds a fit note),
364	then exits without running anything. Hybrid only.
365	
366	```sh
367	./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
368	```
369	
370	```
371	[andesim] hybrid memory map: engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium mem-size=128M
372	REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
373	DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
374	V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
375	ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
376	DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
377	HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
378	SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
379	UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
380	```
381	
382	How to read it:
383	
384	- END is the inclusive last byte.
385	- DRAM tracks `--mem-size`; the V-scratch page above it belongs to andesim.
386	- ILM/DLM/HVM rows appear only when the chosen engine has those memories
387	  and can transport their content; the addresses are the engine's own.
388	- Device state never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART and
389	  SimControl instance); only RAM content does.
390	- Anything NOT listed is unsupported in hybrid mode: it exists in one
391	  engine only, so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.
392	
393	### 5.6 `--dry-run` -- preview without running
394	
395	Valid in every mode: prints the exact engine command line(s), fully
396	resolved and shell-quoted, and runs nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print one
397	command; `hybrid` prints both legs. Use it to see precisely what a run
398	will execute, or to lift the command for your own scripting.
399	
400	```sh
401	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --dry-run my.elf
402	# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
403	# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
404	# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -plugin .../libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=...
405	# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:ax45mpv_premium]
406	# sim_ax45mpv_premium my.elf --resume-from-qemu ... --handoff-out ...
407	```
408	
409	### 5.7 `--verify` -- cross-check a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle
410	
411	A hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
412	(hybrid only, default off) re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
413	exit and compares the architectural state field by field against what the
414	cycle engine drained:
415	
416	```
417	[andesim] 46 cycles
418	[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
419	[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
420	```
421	
422	A mismatch lists each differing field and exits non-zero:
423	
424	```
425	[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
426	[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
427	```
428	
429	What is compared: the PC, all GPRs, FPRs (when FP state is live), the
430	vector registers and V CSRs (when V is live), the privilege level, and the
431	M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff. On an S-mode-capable
432	engine (one whose `--describe` names them, e.g. `vsim:ax66_makatau`) the
433	S/U trap CSRs `satp`, `medeleg`, and `mideleg` also round-trip and are
434	compared. Deliberately excluded: `mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count
435	differently by design), `mip` (hardware-driven pending bits), and a few
436	CSRs whose reset values legitimately differ between engines.
437	
438	Two costs: one extra QEMU run of the whole program (cheap), and a full
439	register read-back over the Debug Module at the ROI exit (not cheap --
440	without `--verify` the exit drain reads only the two counters). Expect a
441	`--verify` run to take noticeably longer; the cycle figure itself is not
442	affected.
443	
444	Related, printed on EVERY hybrid run (not just `--verify`): andesim tracks
445	which config CSRs your program actually wrote during the fast leg and
446	warns if any of them do not exist on the chosen cycle engine:
447	
448	```
449	[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
450	implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
451	hybrid restore skipped them)
452	```
453	
454	That means your program, on that engine's real silicon, would trap before
455	the ROI -- pick an engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes.
456	A clean run prints nothing.
457	
458	### 5.8 `--kanata <file>` (+ `--objdump <file>`) -- pipeline trace of the ROI
459	
460	Hybrid only (`--trigger marker|pc`). Writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace
461	covering exactly the measured window -- engine boot and handoff overhead
462	are filtered out. Open the file in
463	[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata) to see the pipeline.
464	
465	```sh
466	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
467	  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
468	  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
469	```
470	
471	Add `--objdump <file>` (a text dump you generated once with
472	`riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d my.elf > my.S`) and the trace embeds the
473	disassembly next to each PC. `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.
474	
475	Marker-mode constraint: the ELF must contain exactly one exit marker. With
476	more than one, the run errors out and tells you to use `--trigger pc` with
477	an explicit `--pc-end` instead.
478	
479	### 5.9 `--gdb` (+ `--gdb-port <port>`) -- attach a debugger
480	
481	Pauses the simulation at startup so a debugger can attach. Not available
482	in hybrid mode.
483	
484	**fast** -- opens QEMU's GDB stub (default port 1234) and waits:
485	
486	```sh
487	./andesim run --mode fast --gdb my.elf
488	# other terminal:
489	gdb-multiarch -ex 'target remote :1234' my.elf
490	```
491	
492	**cycle** -- resets and HALTS the hart, opens the engine's JTAG bitbang
493	port (default 9104) in the background, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- your JTAG
494	debug server -- in the foreground. Point GDB at the server's own gdb port
495	(from your server config), not at 9104:
496	
497	```sh
498	export ICEMAN=/path/to/jtag-debug-server
499	./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium my.elf
500	```
501	
502	`$ICEMAN` must speak the OpenOCD `remote_bitbang` protocol. A modern
503	**OpenOCD (0.12+)** works: a one-line wrapper can `exec openocd -f <cfg>`
504	where `<cfg>` sets `adapter driver remote_bitbang`, `remote_bitbang port
505	9104`, a generic `riscv` target, and a `gdb_port`. Note: the OpenOCD 0.10
506	bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against this DTM --
507	use a current OpenOCD.
508	
509	`--gdb-port` overrides the port (fast: the QEMU stub port; cycle: the
510	JTAG bitbang port).
511	
512	### 5.10 `--log-level <0-6>` (+ `--log-file`) -- how much andesim says
513	
514	The same scale as the vsim engines' own `--log-level`, so you learn one
515	scheme: `0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off`.
516	Default is `2` (info): you see your program's output, the answer line
517	(`[andesim] N cycles`), and any warnings or errors -- nothing else.
518	
519	`--log-level 1` (debug) adds the driver's chatter: the hybrid banner
520	(engine/VLEN/trigger), the decision lines (which engine and why; what
521	your `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` resolved to), the shared-mmap line (section
522	5.4), the window detail (`[andesim] window: trigger=... vsim mcycle=...
523	qemu mcycle=...`), and the closing PASS line. The level also rides into
524	both hybrid legs: the vsim engine gets the same `--log-level`, the QEMU
525	handoff plugin gets `log_level=`, and their stderr streams live to your
526	terminal (at info and above it is silenced), so one flag tunes the whole
527	pipeline.
528	
529	`--log-level 0` (trace) additionally prints, just before each engine
530	spawns, its fully resolved command line -- the hybrid legs (`[andesim]
531	exec fast-leg [qemu64]: ...`) and the standalone fast/cycle runs
532	(`[andesim] exec standalone [qemu64]: ...`) alike. It is the same text
533	`--dry-run` shows, copy-pasteable to re-run one engine by hand, and it
534	is emitted BEFORE the spawn, so even a hung run leaves the command in
535	the log.
536	
537	`--log-file <file>` appends EVERY level's messages -- timestamped and
538	level-tagged, regardless of the console `--log-level` -- to `<file>`.
539	Run once with `--log-file`, attach the file to a bug report, and nothing
540	needs re-running. Your program's own output is never filtered at any
541	level.
542	
543	Related (always on, any level): when a hybrid leg fails, andesim keeps
544	the run's evidence -- the drained state files, LM sidecars, the staged
545	QEMU config, a copy of your ELF, and a `manifest.txt` with the error and
546	every leg's exact command -- under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` (newest 20
547	kept) and prints where:
548	
549	```
550	[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at /home/u/.cache/andesim/repro/20260711T081500Z-my_prog (see manifest.txt)
551	```
552	
553	### 5.11 `--step-timeout-ms <ms>` -- hybrid only, raise the per-leg timeout
554	
555	Each hybrid leg (the fast QEMU handoff, the cycle-accurate vsim ROI) is
556	spawned with a timeout; the default is `90000` (90s), enough for every
557	fixture-scale ROI. A real, unabridged compute kernel -- a full-size
558	transformer matmul, for instance -- can legitimately need minutes on the
559	~9 kHz cycle-accurate leg. If a hybrid run fails with `plan step N: timed
560	out after <ms> ms`, that is not necessarily a hang: raise the budget and
561	re-run before assuming a bug.
562	
563	```sh
564	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --step-timeout-ms 900000 my.elf
565	```
566	
567	The value must be a positive integer (milliseconds); anything else is a
568	clean `--step-timeout-ms: not a positive integer: <value>` error.
569	
570	### 5.12 `-- <args...>` -- engine passthrough
571	
572	Everything after a bare `--` is forwarded verbatim to the engine.
573	`fast`/`cycle` only: those modes run one engine process, so there is an
574	unambiguous target (see the VLEN example in 5.2). `hybrid` builds both
575	legs' command lines itself and REJECTS `--` args rather than guessing
576	which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
577	`--mem-size`, ...) instead.
578	
579	### 5.13 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel
580	
581	Status: `--mode fast` and `--mode hybrid` (`cycle` is rejected -- no roadmap
582	need for it; see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`).
583	
584	```sh
585	./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
586	```
587	
588	The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
589	private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
590	vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
591	`.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
592	copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
593	`config.env`) to run `objcopy`.
594	
595	Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
596	- `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
597	  the normal way if your app needs more or less.
598	- The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
599	  the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
600	  hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.
601	
602	vlinux loads your app's PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux initial stack
603	(argc/argv/envp/auxv) and jumps to its entry point in M-mode, so it runs like
604	an ordinary freestanding Linux-ABI ELF. `argv[0]` is your app's own path;
605	`-- <args...>` becomes argv[1..] (e.g. `-- -m model.gguf -t 1`), up to 64
606	extra args / 4096 total bytes. envp is always empty -- no test needs it yet.
607	
608	A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
609	`brk` work, `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART, and ordinary
610	host-file I/O works -- `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/`fseek`/`ftell`, `open`/
611	`openat`/`close`/`read`/`pread64`/`lseek`, `fstat`/`fstatat`/`statx` (basic
612	fields: mode, size, nlink, uid/gid), `faccessat`, `getcwd`. Files are opened
613	relative to the engine process's own working directory, same as the vplat
614	runtime's file I/O. Not implemented: symlinks (`readlinkat` always returns
615	`EINVAL`) and directory listing (`getdents64` always returns `ENOSYS`).
616	`clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, `clock_getres`,
617	`nanosleep`/`clock_nanosleep` also work -- the pattern `ggml_time_us()`
618	(llama.cpp's own timing helper) uses -- so timing code compiles and runs
619	unpatched; `nanosleep` returns immediately (there is no timer, so a sleep
620	burns no simulated time) and the values are HOST wall time, meaningful on
621	the fast leg but not inside a vsim ROI (the cycle count is the answer
622	there). File-backed `mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE or MAP_SHARED, PROT_READ, ...)`
623	-- llama.cpp's own GGUF load path uses `MAP_SHARED` -- also works: the
624	file's range is eagerly read into a private, independently-owned copy at
625	mmap time (there is no on-demand paging here, no MMU). A `MAP_SHARED`
626	mapping is only accepted without `PROT_WRITE`: for a read-only mapping
627	there is no observable difference from `MAP_PRIVATE` (the distinction is
628	entirely about write visibility), but a writable `MAP_SHARED` request has
629	no host-file write-back path and is refused (`ENOSYS`). `munmap`
630	(including a partial/tail unmap of an already-mapped range) always
631	succeeds without actually reclaiming space, matching POSIX's own
632	"unmapping unmapped memory is not an error" rule. `mremap` always fails
633	(`ENOMEM`) rather than attempt an in-place grow this allocator cannot do.
634	`sysinfo`, `fadvise64`/`madvise` (access-pattern hints -- there is no
635	readahead/cache policy to tune, so both are accepted no-ops) and `futex`
636	also work: `futex` always answers "available"/"0 waiters", which is safe
637	and spec-legal precisely because there is only one hart -- real
638	concurrency never exists to make that wrong. This does NOT mean threads
639	work: `clone`/`clone3` are `ENOSYS` (no threads,
640	`ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s own non-goal), so `pthread_create` still
641	fails -- code that does not gracefully handle that failure will crash.
642	Known gap:
643	glibc's `exit()` (the library call -- not the raw exit syscall) crashes while
644	running its own internal cleanup-handler list, on what looks like a vendor
645	riscv64 toolchain issue (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U4 for the full
646	investigation); a program that calls the raw `_exit()`/`_Exit()` instead
647	exits cleanly today. Any other unimplemented syscall prints
648	`vlinux: ENOSYS <nr>` once and returns -ENOSYS rather than crashing.
649	
650	**Under `--mode hybrid`**: `--trigger marker` works --
651	`<andesim/ROI.h>`'s `andesim_ROI_begin()`/`andesim_ROI_end()` around any
652	region of your app measures it cycle-accurately, exactly like a bare-metal
653	marker'd fixture. One thing happens automatically that is worth knowing:
654	vsim's own trigger only scans the ELF it is told to BOOT (here, the staged
655	vlinux-run.elf) for the marker instructions -- but the markers are in
656	YOUR app, which vlinux only loads into memory at runtime, never part of
657	vlinux-run.elf's own static content. andesim resolves your app's real
658	exit-marker address itself and passes it to vsim directly, so this is
659	transparent -- you do not need `--trigger pc` or to know the address
660	yourself. `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` here too. See section 11 for a
661	full walkthrough building up to a real llama.cpp kernel measurement.
662	Track progress in `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`.

666	## 6. The `profile` command -- find your ROI first
667	
668	When you do not yet know WHERE the hot region is, run `profile` before
669	`run --mode hybrid`:
670	
671	```sh
672	./andesim profile [--engine <id>] my_kernel.elf
673	```
674	
675	It runs the whole ELF under QEMU with a loop-detector plugin
676	(`libhotIterationLoop.so`) and prints a Markdown report of the hottest
677	loops. Each loop block ends with a ready window:
678	
679	```
680	measure:      --pc-start 0x10007c --pc-end 0x1000c2  (all of vadd_kernel: entry -> ret)
681	```
682	
683	Paste that pair into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` to
684	measure exactly that function on the cycle engine.
685	
686	profile picks its engine the same way hybrid does (`--engine <id>`, or
687	the sole installed cycle-accurate engine) and launches QEMU with THAT
688	engine's configuration -- the same `-cpu`/`-readconfig` sync a hybrid
689	fast leg gets. So the loop ranking reflects the ISA (including VLEN) of
690	the engine you will measure on.
691	
692	Useful knobs: `--min-iters <N>` drops cold loops, `--limit <N>` caps the
693	report, `--no-optimize-rvv` also shows scalar loops (the default reports
694	RVV-containing loops only), `--no-llm` prints a plain table, `--dry-run`
695	previews the QEMU command. Full reference: `docs/profile.md`.

699	## 7. What a hybrid run does for you automatically
700	
701	You normally do not need this section to use andesim -- it explains the
702	behaviors you will observe.
703	
704	**Two legs, one state.** The fast leg (QEMU) runs to your ROI start, then
705	drains the complete architectural state -- GPRs, FPRs, vector registers,
706	CSRs (including the Andes-specific blocks), privilege level -- into a
707	state file. Program RAM is shared by construction (both legs map the same
708	file), so memory needs no copy. The cycle engine restores the state
709	through its Debug Module, runs your ROI, and drains the counters at the
710	exit trigger. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta.
711	
712	**Config that matters for timing rides along.** Cache-enable state (L1
713	`mcache_ctl`, and the L2 controller's config window on engines that have
714	an L2) is restored before the ROI, so a program that enabled caches during
715	boot measures WITH caches on -- not at the engine's reset default.
716	
717	**Only what your program wrote is restored.** andesim records which config
718	CSRs the program actually wrote during the fast leg and restores only
719	those; an untouched CSR keeps the engine's own reset value, exactly like
720	that engine's real silicon. If the program wrote a CSR the engine does not
721	implement, you get the warning shown in section 5.7.
722	
723	**Local memories travel too.** On engines with ILM/DLM (tightly-coupled
724	memories) or HVM (high-bandwidth vector memory), their content is drained
725	from the fast leg and loaded into the cycle engine before resume, so a
726	program that stages code or data there before the ROI resumes with it in
727	place. (A program using ILM/DLM must enable them itself via
728	`milmb`/`mdlmb`, as real TCM firmware does; that write is restored
729	automatically.) `--print-memmap` shows whether your engine has these
730	regions.
731	
732	**First-run baseline capture.** Restoring a register over the Debug Module
733	costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most state still holds reset
734	values. The first hybrid run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair captures
735	the engine's reset state once and caches it under `~/.cache/andesim/`
736	(honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); later runs skip the no-op restores, typically
737	cutting the vsim leg ~4x. The cache invalidates itself when the engine or
738	ELF changes; delete the directory to force a fresh capture. This never
739	changes results -- a restore is skipped only when the value is already
740	there.
741	
742	**The ROI envelope (limits).** The measured window is assumed bare-metal,
743	single-hart, trap-free, interrupt-free, paging-off, and single-privilege.
744	The S/U trap CSRs `satp`, `medeleg`, and `mideleg` are transported on
745	S-mode-capable engines (so an in-ROI read sees your values); other S-mode
746	CSRs (`sstatus`, `sepc`, ...) are not transported yet. The privilege level
747	itself IS carried: an S/U-mode handoff also mirrors the PMP configuration
748	and requires an S/U-capable engine -- on an M-mode-only engine the resume
749	aborts with a clear pick-another-engine error. A workload that traps,
750	takes an interrupt, or switches privilege inside the ROI is outside the
751	contract. And because there is no hand-back leg, nothing after the ROI
752	executes.

792	## 9. Troubleshooting
793	
794	| Symptom | Meaning / fix |
795	|---------|----------------|
796	| `multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: ...)` | More than one engine is installed. Add `--engine <id>` from `list engines`. |
797	| `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64 -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF` | Width mismatch caught up front. Rebuild the ELF for the engine's width or pick the other engine. |
798	| `--trigger marker\|pc is required (the ROI delimiter; ...)` | Hybrid always needs the ROI delimiter: `--trigger marker` (markers in source) or `--trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E`. |
799	| The run never reaches the ROI / hangs until timeout | The start trigger never fired: the binary has no markers (marker mode), or `--pc-start` is never executed. Check with `--trigger pc` on a PC you know retires, or run `./andesim profile` to find real hot PCs. |
800	| `symbol '<x>' not defined in <elf>` / `malformed address '<x>'` | `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` must be a defined symbol or a valid `0x` literal. |
801	| `--pc-start and --pc-end resolve to the same address ... (an empty ROI measures nothing)` | Pick two distinct boundaries; equal ones would measure nothing. |
802	| `--mem-size ...` rejected, or `raise --mem-size or shrink the image` | Hybrid caps at `2G` minus 4 KiB (use `2047M`), and the ELF's static image must fit below the reserved V-scratch page. |
803	| The mmap chose a disk directory (`[andesim] mmap ...` at `--log-level 1`), or `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` run fails | `/dev/shm` was too small for the request. Either accept the disk tier, free RAM, or pin a big non-tmpfs directory via `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`. |
804	| `warning: the program wrote CSRs engine ... does not implement: ...` | The figure may not represent this program on this engine (on silicon those writes would trap). Choose an engine implementing those CSRs, or drop the writes. |
805	| `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` (with `--kanata`) | Kanata needs a unique exit; switch to `--trigger pc` and name the exit with `--pc-end`. |
806	| `hybrid` rejects `-- <args>` | By design: hybrid owns both legs' command lines. Use the dedicated flags instead. |
807	| Missing artifact / engine not discovered | Run `./andesim doctor`; it names exactly what is missing and where it looked. Setup/build is covered in `README.md`. |
808	| A hybrid leg failed and you want to report or debug it | The run printed `[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at <dir>` -- that directory holds the evidence and `manifest.txt` has each leg's exact command (newest 20 kept). Re-run with `--log-file run.log` (and `--log-level 1` for live engine logs) for the full picture. |

826	
827	`ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U8: a real static-glibc `llama-completion`

832	> The capital of France is Paris. Paris is the second-largest city in
833	> France, with a population of over 1.8 million. Paris is located in the
834	> Île-de-France

836	(Bonsai-4B-Q1_0 is an extreme 1-bit quantization -- "second-largest" is a
837	model-quality artifact, not an andesim/vlinux correctness issue; the
838	point here is that a real 4B-parameter model's real GGUF loading,
839	tokenization, RVV matrix math, and sampling all produced coherent,
840	on-topic English text end to end.) This needs the vendor static-glibc

844	### Build
845	
846	A fresh **static** build, separate from any dynamic build you may already
847	have (a dynamic build cannot run here -- there is no dynamic linker under
848	vlinux):
849	
850	```sh
851	TC=$LINUX_TOOLCHAIN   # the static-glibc toolchain, config.env's LINUX_TOOLCHAIN
852	cmake -B build-rv64-static \
853	  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
854	  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc \
855	  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++ \
856	  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
857	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg \
858	  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
859	  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
860	  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
861	  -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
862	  -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS=ON
863	
864	cmake --build build-rv64-static -j$(nproc) --target llama-completion
865	```
866	
867	What each non-obvious flag is for:
868	- `-static` (the linker flag, not just `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`): without
869	  it the binary still dynamically links libc/libstdc++/the dynamic
870	  linker itself -- there is no dynamic linker under vlinux, so this is
871	  required, not optional.
872	- `-mext-zvlsseg`: the Andes toolchain gates RVV segment-load/store
873	  intrinsics behind this flag; ggml's RVV kernels use them.
874	- `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`: the target engine (`ax45mpv_premium`,
875	  ELEN=32) has no scalar or vector half-precision float support; leaving
876	  these on produces code that traps.
877	- `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`: repacking picks tensor layouts tuned for
878	  specific microarchitectures vlinux is not modeling.
879	- `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`: no OpenMP runtime here. This does NOT remove
880	  threading -- ggml's CPU backend still spawns its own thread pool via
881	  `pthread_create` when `-t` asks for more than one thread. vlinux has no
882	  `clone`/`clone3` support (no threads, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md's own
883	  non-goal), so **always pass `-t 1`** at run time.
884	- `LLAMA_CURL=OFF`: no network stack here; only needed for llama.cpp's
885	  optional model-download-by-URL feature.
886	
887	**One required source patch**, independent of `-t 1`: llama.cpp's own
888	async status logger (`common/log.cpp`) spawns a background `std::thread`
889	unconditionally, on the FIRST log call, regardless of `-t` -- and the
890	generated completion text itself is printed through this same logger
891	(`LOG("%s", token_str.c_str())`), not a separate direct-stdout path, so
892	it cannot simply be avoided or ignored. Since `clone` is `ENOSYS` here,
893	that `std::thread` construction throws `std::system_error`, uncaught,
894	crashing the process before `main()`'s own code ever runs. This is a
895	genuine upstream robustness gap (a background-logging performance
896	optimization should not be able to crash the whole program if thread
897	creation fails, on ANY platform), not a vlinux-specific issue -- fixed by
898	catching the construction failure in `common_log::resume()` and falling
899	back to printing synchronously from `add()` instead of queueing for a
900	worker that will never run. Apply this patch to your llama.cpp checkout
901	before building:
902	
903	```diff
904	--- a/common/log.cpp
905	+++ b/common/log.cpp
906	@@ struct common_log {
907	     bool prefix;
908	     bool timestamps;
909	     bool running;
910	+    bool synchronous = false; // true if the worker thread could not be
911	+                              // created (e.g. no thread support on this
912	+                              // platform) -- add() prints inline instead
913	@@ void add(...) {
914	         ...
915	         entry.timestamp = 0;
916	         if (timestamps) {
917	             entry.timestamp = t_us() - t_start;
918	         }
919	
920	+        if (synchronous) {
921	+            // No worker thread exists (see resume()) -- print immediately
922	+            // rather than queueing for a consumer that will never run.
923	+            print_entry(entry);
924	+            return;
925	+        }
926	+
927	         tail = (tail + 1) % queue.size();
928	         cv_new.notify_one();
929	     }
930	
931	     void resume() {
932	         ...
933	         running = true;
934	
935	-        thrd = std::thread([this]() {
936	-            ...
937	-        });
938	+        try {
939	+            thrd = std::thread([this]() {
940	+                ...
941	+            });
942	+        } catch (const std::system_error &) {
943	+            synchronous = true;
944	+        }
945	     }
946	
947	     void pause() {
948	         {
949	             ...
950	             running = false;
951	
952	+            if (synchronous) {
953	+                return; // no worker thread exists to signal/join
954	+            }
955	+
956	             // push an entry to signal the worker thread to stop
957	             ...
958	```
959	
960	(the `...` markers stand for unchanged surrounding code; see
961	`common/log.cpp`'s `add()`/`resume()`/`pause()` methods for exact
962	context.)

997	### Measuring one kernel iteration under hybrid mode
998	
999	The fast leg above proves correctness; `--mode hybrid` measures real
1000	cycles for one kernel iteration -- a full token would take hours at
1001	vsim's cycle-accurate clock (~9 kHz) even for a model this size, which is
1002	why hybrid mode exists: everything up to the marker runs on the fast
1003	QEMU leg (negligible time), and only the marked region runs on the
1004	cycle-accurate leg.

1006	```sh
1007	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
1008	  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
1009	  build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
1010	  -- -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
1011	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
1012	```

1014	(`--mem-size` stays under 2G -- the AE350 DRAM window's actual usable
1015	ceiling is 2 GiB minus the V-scratch reservation, so `2000M` not `2G`.
1016	`--step-timeout-ms` raises the per-leg spawn timeout past its 90s
1017	default -- a real matmul on the cycle-accurate leg needs minutes; see the

1023	builds its whole computation graph before executing it in one shot,
1024	individual operations are not distinguishable at the application call-site
1025	level (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code) -- the markers go in ggml's
1026	own generic per-node dispatch loop instead, gated by a counter so only
1027	one specific node's execution is actually measured.
